beats.intro: Unit four begins the move from arithmetic to algebra. [[q]]The first tool is a shorthand for repeated multiplication: the exponent.
beats.define: Four times four times four is a lot to write. [[short]]Instead, write four with a small three raised beside it. [[base]]The four is the base: the number being multiplied. [[exp]]The three is the exponent: how many copies of the base you multiply. [[read]]Read it as four to the third power, or four cubed. [[val]]Four times four is sixteen, and sixteen times four is sixty-four.
beats.square: Why cubed? [[sq]]Three squared is three times three: the number of unit squares in a three by three square. That's nine. [[cube]]And three cubed is three times three times three: the number of unit cubes in a three by three by three cube. [[layers]]Three layers of nine make twenty-seven.
beats.oneZero: Two special exponents. [[one]]An exponent of one means one copy of the base, so seven to the first power is just seven. [[pat]]Now look at this pattern. Two to the fourth is sixteen. [[p3]]Two cubed is eight. [[p2]]Two squared is four. [[p1]]Two to the first is two. [[step]]Each time the exponent goes down by one, you divide by two. [[p0]]So two to the zero must be one. [[rule]]Any nonzero number to the zero power is one.
beats.negBase: Be careful with negative numbers. [[q]]In negative two, in parentheses, to the fourth, the parentheses make negative two the base. [[calc]]Negative two times itself four times: four negative signs, so the answer is positive sixteen. [[q2]]But in negative two to the fourth without parentheses, the base is only the two. [[calc2]]Two to the fourth is sixteen, and the minus sign stays in front: negative sixteen. [[rule]]Always ask: what exactly is the base?
beats.negExp: The pattern keeps going below zero. [[p0]]Two to the zero is one. [[pm1]]Divide by two again: two to the negative one is one half. [[pm2]]Two to the negative two is one quarter. [[rule]]A negative exponent means the reciprocal: two to the negative n is one over two to the n. [[ex]]So three to the negative two is one over three squared, one ninth. [[sign]]A negative exponent does not make the number negative.
beats.fracExp: For a fraction with a negative exponent, flip the fraction and make the exponent positive. [[q]]Three quarters to the negative two [[flip]]becomes four thirds squared, [[ans]]which is sixteen ninths.
beats.wrap: An exponent tells how many copies of the base to multiply. [[w1]]To the first power is the number itself, and to the zero power is one. [[w2]]Parentheses decide the base: negative two to the fourth in parentheses is positive, without them it's negative. [[w3]]A negative exponent means take the reciprocal. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final2: Next, decide whether each value is positive, negative, or between zero and one.
beats.final3: Last one. Decide whether each statement is true or false.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter nineteen, exponents.
